title: Guiding chart Y axis draws two labels on top of each other when the series is flat
reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Seeded Night C - M31 with three frames all at guiding_rms_total = 0.70; the Guiding performance axis renders '0.25' and '0.20' printed on top of each other at the bottom of the axis (evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2a-08-guideaxis-070.png, native-resolution crop). Root cause is at the cited location: chart_axis.dart:31-43, the zero-variance branch returns min = centre - interval*2 (0.70-0.50 = 0.20), which is NOT a multiple of the interval (0.25), so fl_chart's boundary label lands a fraction of a tick from the outermost tick - the exact failure the class doc-comment says NiceAxis exists to prevent (the non-degenerate branch below it snaps min/max to interval multiples; the degenerate branch does not). Not unique to guiding: with a 0.60 series the same branch prints '1.10' touching '1.00', and Focus drift prints '15240' touching '15200'.

title: BLS card gives no significance verdict, and its only significance number (SDE) scores pure noise higher than a textbook-strong periodic signal
location_wrong: period_analysis_service.dart:604-621 (the SDE formula) is right. The UI half is not in period_analysis_panel/result_widgets.dart - that file only defines _ResultColumn/_Verdict rendering; the decision of whether a BLS verdict is shown is period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599 (blsVerdict) and the SDE string is built at :620.
reasoning: The substantive half fully reproduces, checked by INDEPENDENT recomputation rather than by trusting the app: I ported computeBls (period_analysis_service.dart:445-637) to Python and ran it on three 80-point, 118.5-minute light curves at 90 s cadence with the app's own parameters (minP 0.01 d, maxP = 0.0823 d baseline, nbins 200, err 0.008). The port reproduces the app's on-screen noise result exactly (app: 31.4 min / 1.9 min / -54.1 mmag / SDE 3.11; port: 31.408 min / 1.885 min / -54.05 mmag / SDE 3.112), which validates it. Results: (A) pure gaussian noise sigma=0.03 -> SDE 3.11; (B) injected sinusoid P=20 min amplitude 0.10 mag -> best period 21.0 min, SDE 2.56; (C) injected box transit P=20 min depth +0.150 mag -> best period 19.9 min, depth +153.9 mmag, SDE 4.80. So pure noise (3.11) still outscores a strong injected periodic signal (2.56), and a genuine transit reaches only 4.80 - below the code's own documented significance threshold (':81 SDE > ~6 is typically considered a significant detection'). Same ordering and conclusion as the claim's 2.7 / 2.5 / 4.82. PARTIAL FIX SINCE FILING: the panel now does compute a BLS verdict (period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599: sde > 7 -> Strong, sde > 6 -> Noteworthy), so 'no verdict of any kind' is no longer literally true - but because a real transit only scores 4.8 on this implementation, the badge never fires in practice and the card still shows a bare 'SDE: 3.11' with no threshold beside it (live: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2a-19-bls.png).

title: "Box Least Squares (Transit Search)" reports negative transit depths, i.e. it presents a brightening as a transit

My independent port confirms the sign is data-driven and unconstrained: noise -54.05 mmag, injected sinusoid -106.6 mmag, injected +0.150 mag box +153.9 mmag. Cited code is right (a couple of lines off): SR = s^2/(r(1-r)) is maximised at period_analysis_service.dart:537-545 and is sign-blind, and globalBestDepth = inTransitMean - outTransitMean is set at :599 (claim said :597) with no sign constraint.

title: Diagnostics tab shows loading skeletons forever for a session it cannot analyse
location_wrong: The claim's diagnosis - 'the no-solved-frames path never completes' - is wrong, and would send a fixer looking for a guard that is not the problem. I disproved it with a control: Night A - M31 has ZERO plate-solved frames, zero psf_field_tiles and zero residual vectors, and its Diagnostics view resolves immediately to a full 'Optical Health / Not measured' result. Night D - V-Test (plate-solved, 20 psf tiles, 0 residuals) also resolves. Only Night E - M13 hangs, and its distinguishing property is that the Analytics > Science tab had already subscribed to sessionPsfTilesProvider(5) / sessionResidualVectorsProvider(5). The suspect is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/optical_train_diagnostics_provider.dart:31-38, where _watchScienceRows composes via the deprecated `ref.watch(provider.stream)`; that forwards only FUTURE events, so a source stream that already emitted before this subscription leaves psfAsync/residualsAsync permanently isLoading, and :65-67 then returns AsyncValue.loading() forever.
reasoning: Symptom reproduced twice, deterministically: Analytics > Diagnostics > 'Night E - M13' renders five shimmer skeletons and never resolves. I waited over 100 s, re-read the accessibility tree three times (it ends at 'Learn more about optical diagnostics' with no result text at all), and 'log --tail 25' shows only routine discovery lines - no error. Re-selecting Night E after a working session reproduced the hang immediately. Severity stays P2: an indefinite skeleton with no error is indistinguishable from a hang, and it is triggered by the ordinary path of looking at Science and then Diagnostics for the same night.
